executive_summary: A lightweight, grep-optimized memory system that enables agents to build contextual understanding through structured logs, indexed memories, and semantic search patterns. Designed to scale to 100+ agents while maintaining sub-100ms search performance using only Claude SDK tools.

directory_structure.description: Each agent gets memories/agents/{agent-id}/ with standardized subdirectories

memories/agents/{agent-id}/.performance_log.json: Task execution history with metrics (already exists)

tasks/.{task-id}.json: Complete task record including inputs, outputs, errors, learnings
tasks/.index.json: Fast lookup index: {task_id -> {timestamp, type, status, tags}}

relationships/.collaborations.jsonl: Log of interactions with other agents

metadata/.stats.json: Current statistics: task counts, success rates, specialization metrics
metadata/.reputation_score.json: Reputation tracking (already exists in some agents)

example_researcher.content:
# Researcher Domain Knowledge

## Best Practices
- Always cite sources with URLs
- Cross-reference multiple sources (minimum 3)
- Check publication dates (prefer 2024-2025 for tech)
- Verify claims with official documentation

## Tools & Techniques
- WebSearch: Use specific queries like 'FastAPI 2025 benchmarks' not 'FastAPI info'
- WebFetch: For deep-diving into specific documentation pages
- Always check official GitHub repos for latest statistics

## Common Pitfalls
- Outdated benchmarks (verify year)
- Marketing claims vs real-world performance
- Single-source bias

solution_1_rolling_windows.description: Keep recent context fresh, archive old

100_agents_scenario.concurrent_access: No locking needed - each agent has own directory, reads are always safe, writes are to own files only

growth_rate.week_1: 100 agents * 10 tasks * 50KB = 50 MB new task data
growth_rate.conclusion: Easily manageable, can run on single SSD indefinitely

pros: ✓ Uses only Claude SDK tools (Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob) - no external dependencies
✓ Fast searches with grep/glob - sub-second for common queries
✓ Scales to 100+ agents with predictable performance (~330 MB for 100 agents)
✓ JSONL format is append-friendly and grep-optimized
✓ Hierarchical search (fast → deep) optimizes for common case
✓ Integrates seamlessly with existing Task delegation
✓ Works with existing memory structure (extends, doesn't replace)
✓ Agent autonomy - each agent manages own memories
✓ Low overhead - ~10-20% time on memory operations
✓ Enables learning and improvement over time
cons: ✗ Requires discipline to maintain (agents must follow post-task protocol)
✗ Manual consolidation triggers (could be automated with cron jobs, but requires setup)
✗ Grep searches are linear time O(n) - not indexed database queries
✗ No semantic search (only keyword/regex matching) - can't find 'similar' concepts
✗ JSON/JSONL parsing overhead for large files
✗ File I/O can be slow on network filesystems (requires local SSD)
✗ No built-in conflict resolution (if agents somehow write to same file simultaneously)
✗ Memory consolidation requires agent to review own memories (meta-task)
✗ Tag consistency depends on agent discipline (typos break grep)
✗ Cross-agent search gets slower as agent count grows (linear in agent count)
✗ No automatic memory pruning - requires conscious consolidation
✗ Large grep operations can spike CPU briefly
✗ No built-in versioning of memory files (depends on git)

conclusion: The Hierarchical Context-Aware Memory System (HCAMS) provides a practical, scalable solution for agent memory using only Claude SDK tools. It balances simplicity with power, enabling agents to build contextual understanding over time while maintaining fast search performance. The tiered search strategy optimizes for common cases (recent work) while still supporting deep historical searches. The consolidation strategy prevents unbounded growth. Integration with Task delegation is seamless. This system will enable the AI civilization to learn and improve continuously.
recommendation: IMPLEMENT Phase 1-2 immediately for 10 existing agents, monitor for 1 week, then roll out Phase 3-4 based on learnings.
